Anyway, in this dream, my brother and father and I are sitting around the bbq pit we had in our old backyard. My dad loved to smoke meat, drink beer, sit outside, and just read, or sharpen his pocket knife. They both looked like they did before they died, and I looked like I do now.

So we are talking and laughing. They are drinking. I'm not. My dad reaches to a nearby table and grabs a homemade tortilla from a plate, opens the pit, cuts a fatty piece of brisket off with his pocket knife, wraps the meat in a tortilla and hands it to me. As a kid, I had the same dream almost every single night for what must have been months, it was the strangest thing. I became afraid to go to sleep. The dream itself wasn't too out of the ordinary -- the repetition was the strangest thing about it for me. Every dream would begin with me walking down the hall, approaching my room. I could see my mom in there, with the lights on, ready to read me a bedtime story (I was pretty young at the time). When I crossed the threshold, I suddenly found that it wasn't my room at all, but the study across the hall. The door would close behind me and big, hairy monsters resembling Chewbacca would swarm me and kill me, ending the dream.

The coolest part about the whole thing is how the dreams ended, seemingly for no reason. About a week after they ended, I had a pretty innocuous dream where I was in the hallway again, but it was daytime. My mom was upstairs with me and the vacuum was running downstairs. I asked her if Dad was vacuuming, and she said he wasn't home (I have no siblings). Confused, I looked downstairs to find a Chewie monster vacuuming our foyer, who waved at me cheerfully. Weirdest dream I ever had.

31 30 32 30 34 32 31 30 Humanity has come a long way it seems. We've learned how to reach out and touch the galaxy and soon the Universe. Not me though, I just make the food.

I'm what you'd call a cook I suppose, what you're reading right now is my journal I've been keeping for the last few years, seeing as I do quite a bit of traveling these days. Work is plentiful across this arm of the galaxy and I don't need to look far if I don't want to. There are some pretty fun ways to make money being a cook.
For example the time I took a gig with a small exploratory crew. If you have the credentials and training to make a decent meal in the bush you can earn a few credits. It's really about how much gear you can pack. They know the food won't be something they'd get in a restaurant, they're tough-guys after all. I did get some weapons training once, the course was cheap and I had some spare time, two days and I have my license galactically to carry a small firearm or equivalent low to zero atmosphere capable weapon. Was pretty cheap too.

So we head to this planet, I don't remember the co-ordinates right now but it was just near the Orion system I think. Well we landed fine, no issues en-route pretty mundane all in all but I tell you, when I stepped outside the ship and got a good look through my visor it was quite an astounding view.

The first thing you notice is the color, all a purple blue. Y'know how all plants on earth are pretty well green, grass trees that sort of thing? Well here its all purple and blue. And instead of trees there are enormous mushrooms taller than some buildings. Then you notice its not all plants and mushrooms, there are these faint almost transparent jelly-fish creatures, they just kinda bob along and done seem to pay no mind. We made some headway towards some caverns and set up our equipment and a small shelter to contain an atmosphere and set up the heater for cooking, its just a simple induction plate to heat water to make general rations and the like. If they pay me enough I bring my own “rations” that I prepare beforehand and freeze dry. They're not bad if I do say so myself.

We usually only go for a day or so, and the meals we eat are enough to be a days worth of calories so we only stop once for food. Maybe twice. I have done month long journeys but we usually have a way to carry supplies at that point and bring a mobile kitchen set up and a few rations as well as a bit of fresh food, logistically we've had food drops too its pretty good for the crew and the moral. Sometimes we have to feed 5 guys, sometimes 100, but luckily those contracts have more than one of us. That's kinda hit and miss too, I keep to one man jobs these days.

You could call me a freelancer I guess. It pays the bills, I got a pretty sweet shack out in a quiet part of the solar system. A decent little jumpship for when I wanna take a vacation. Some suckers pay way too much money for food, it's not a bad life at all.

Well I think that's it for today for this entry. Eat well kids

Talasheem keeled down and placed a finger in the tepid water. Rubbing his finger tip to his lips, he felt the tingle of the mushtree's toxins. It wasn't enough to harm him, but the water wasn't safe to drink. Looking around him he could see the mushtrees spreading throughout the valley. They were becoming more numerous as Tala travels farther down from the Deep Forest. With a backwards glance at the green walls that rose miles above his head, Tala decided it was time to make haste.

The sun was starting to set behind the distant plans. Tala had made good time, and was now deep into the mushtree swamp. He could hear the soft, deep moans of the mushtree seeds. Their blue, jelly like bodies and tendrils refracted the sunset's light, making it dance. He was careful to avoid them when one drifted close to him. Remembering the time, as a child Singer, he was one come down on a trader's pack animal. It landed on the two legged kree and instantly rooted itself to the creature and the soil. The kree's crys haunted him some nights.

Tala stepped up near a cliff outcropping, gazing down into the river. The blue glow from the blub fungus shown brightly in the evening light. It wasn't much farther to the river itself, then from there, the valley exit. Across the gap, he saw two kree traveling in the same direction as himself. As Tala watched, the larger kree let out a loud trumpeting. The smaller ran to catch up to what looked to be it's parent. The loud sounds meant that he needed to hurry. Kree weren't known for being bright, and as such made good meals. It was best to not be near when something was close enough to attack. Picking up his pace again, Talasheem wondered aloud softly;

"Why did I have to leave? Why did the Elders send me to travel through such a place?"
